claim: ASML's 2025 net system sales were EUR 24,474 million (about EUR 24.5 billion; EUV EUR 11.6bn, DUV EUR 12.0bn, metrology & inspection EUR 825m), alongside Installed Base Management sales of EUR 8.2 billion.
evidence: "2025 Net system sales €24,474 million 2024 Net system sales €21,769 million" (p. 9); "EUV system sales increased 39% to €11.6 billion"; "DUV system sales decreased 6% to €12.0 billion"; "Metrology & Inspection systems sales increased 28% to €825 million"; "Installed Base Management sales increased 26% to €8.2 billion" (p. 7)

metric.name: ASML net system sales
metric.population: ASML net system sales (EUV + DUV + metrology & inspection); excludes Installed Base Management

notes: Corrects CLM-0509, which gave new system sales as EUR 24.6bn; the deck gives EUR 24,474m. Found by fact-check fc-W0-70bd.

claim: TrendForce estimated TSMC's 2Q26 foundry revenue at nearly US$40.2 billion, a 72.5% foundry market share (Samsung 5.9%, SMIC 5.4%); the shares are measured against a foundry total larger than the US$53.49 billion top-10 combined revenue.
evidence: "TSMC maintained its lead with 2Q26 revenue nearing $40.2 billion, a 12.1% increase QoQ, capturing a 72.5% market share."; "the combined revenue of the world's top 10 foundries rose 11.5% QoQ to nearly US$53.49 billion in 2Q26"; Samsung "Revenue edged up 1.8% QoQ to $3.26 billion ... market share declined to 5.9%"

metric.name: TSMC foundry market share
metric.population: TrendForce foundry market total (denominator not stated; implied about US$55bn, i.e. larger than the top-10 sum)

notes: 40.2/53.49 = 75.2%, 3.26/53.49 = 6.1%; the published 72.5% and 5.9% both imply a denominator of about US$55.3-55.4bn, so the shares are not shares of the top-10 combined revenue as CLM-0553 states.

claim: SIA's summary of the 2024 SIA/BCG report puts the US share of global fab capacity at 37% in 1990, 12% in 2020 and 10% as of 2022.
evidence: "The U.S. share of global fab capacity has experienced a multi-decade decline, decreasing from 37% in 1990 to 12% in 2020, and further declining to 10% as of 2022." (p. 2); FIG 2: "Global 200mm+ commercial semiconductor fab capacity share by region, 1990-2032F"

metric.name: US share of global fab capacity

notes: Newer and better-defined than the June 2021 White House 'production' figure (12% 'today'), which the same report (p. 37) describes as manufacturing capacity.

notes: Supersedes the circa-2020 USD 150m figure in CLM-0482; consistent with Reuters ~USD 250m (CLM-1751).

evidence: "A leading-edge 2nm-class fab module with a capacity of roughly 20,000 wafer starts per month costs roughly $25 billion to $35 billion to build and equip"
